core_summary: This chapter covers equal sharing, unit fractions 1/n, numerators and denominators, fraction wall visual representations, equivalent fractions, proper/improper/mixed fractions, number line placement, and Brahmagupta's general formulas (628 CE) for fraction addition and subtraction.
key_concepts: Fraction Definition: In a/b, 'a' represents numerator (selected equal parts) and 'b' represents denominator (total equal parts in whole).
Unit Fraction Inversion: A unit fraction 1/n decreases in physical magnitude as the denominator n increases (1/8 < 1/3).
Equivalent Fraction Scaling: Multiplying or dividing numerator and denominator by the same non-zero integer preserves fraction value.
Mixed to Improper Conversion: Mixed fraction A b/c converts to improper fraction (A x c + b) / c.
Brahmagupta's Addition Formula: a/b + c/d = (a.d + b.c) / (b.d).
Brahmagupta's Subtraction Formula: a/b - c/d = (a.d - b.c) / (b.d).

key_terms.definition: A number representing equal parts of a whole or equal division of a quantity.
A fraction with a numerator of 1, representing one equal part of a divided whole.
Fractions that express the same proportion or value despite having different numerators and denominators.
A fraction whose numerator is greater than or equal to its denominator.
A number represented as a combination of a whole integer and a proper fraction.

key_takeaways: Adding or subtracting fractions requires converting them to equivalent fractional units with common denominators.
Brahmagupta's formulas provide an elegant general method for fraction arithmetic without explicit LCM finding.
Larger denominators mean smaller individual fractional parts when dividing a single whole.
